node.label: Gordon S. Wood
node.date_label: The Creation of the American Republic (1969) · Empire of Liberty (2009) · Power and Liberty (2021)
node.description: Historian of the American Revolution whose account joins republican ideas to changes in social authority. In an interview published posthumously in2026,Wood contrasts monarchical patronage with popular sovereignty and traces competing notions of representation. His interpretation of revolutionary transformation is influential and contested; broad claims of democratic modernity do not erase slavery or unequal inclusion.

incident_edges.relationship: Wood connects republican transformation to changes in patronage,deference and social dependence.
incident_edges.evidence_note: Own interview opening on monarchy as a social hierarchy; his transformative thesis is attributed and does not establish equal freedom for all.

incident_edges.relationship: Wood recalls Bailyn’s seminar teaching him historical-mindedness as a way of understanding rather than accumulating facts.
